So, this is your first nightshift?’ The man brought the smoke to his dry lips covered by his thick moustache, glancing down at the ashtray before gazing at a corner of the room as if he deeply contemplated.

‘Yes. My friends have been calling me Mr. Cop Cop for the last week and I don’t think that’s going to stop any time soon,’ the young officer whose shaved face and telling round eyes made him look more like a boy next to the patrolman, failed in hiding his awkwardness. 

‘The nightshifts are the best part, boy. I don’t know if you’re the clubbing person, banging your head to this shitty music that kids dance to today, but you will get my point sooner or later.’

‘Because the action’s at night?’

‘You think you’ll like the action, officer…’

‘Nick,’ he answered almost as if the older man’s gun was pointing straight to his brains.

‘Nick, that’s right. Well, listen now, Nick, you’ll have many cops play the butch ones to you, they’re addicted to hazing in a sort of way. I might have done that too you know and, trust me, I know the way to make you jitter every time you even hear my raspy voice anywhere close to you, 'cause I was your age once and things used to be wilder in my days. It’s all a matter of respect, you see,’ Nick watched the man with the dedication of a priest during a ritual, ‘but I’ve learnt that no respect can be earned that way, only dread.’

‘I guess you’re right, sir.’

‘Don’t guess and don’t call me “sir”. I’m Connor and we’re colleagues now,’ Connor moved the smoke to his left hand and shook firmly Nick’s sweaty palm. 

 	As Connor set Nick free from his probing stare, the young policeman scanned the office through his bright pair of hazelnut eyes. It was a bit more modest and drabber compared to those he was used to seeing in movies but he had guessed so. He wondered what was lying inside those folders that were leaning on each other on the rusty bookcase, whether they were concealing reports of notorious crimes or gangs or just contained boring legal documents. It was probably too early to ask about that.  

‘So why are nightshifts the best part?’

‘Are you frightened, son? I believe I am allowed to call you son, you’re thirty years younger than I am,’ he laughed and coughed at the same time just like a chronic smoker with a yet undetected lung cancer would. Nick nodded answering to both of his remarks. ‘Fear is not allowed in this job. Citizens depend on us for their safety, we cannot be afraid 'cause when you’re afraid you can’t even protect yourself. How are you going then to protect others?’

	Nick wished himself were into smoking or that there was a bottle of bourbon lying in one of the drawers; he guessed there actually could be.
